ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Proposed Criminal Revision has 
been filed challenging the impugned 
order dated 23.03.2023, by which, 
the Application for Interim 
Maintenance, filed by the respondent 
no.2, has been allowed. Proposed 
Criminal Revision has been filed along 
with an Application under Section 5 of 
the Limitation Act, 1963 to condone 
the delay of 35 days in preferring the 
Revision.
2. Heard Mr. Himanshu Pal, learned 
counsel (through video conferencing) 
with Mr. Prasanna Karnatak, learned 
counsel for the revisionist.
3. Issue notice to the respondent no.2 
on Delay Condonation Application (IA 
No.2 of 2023). Steps to be taken within 
three days. 
4. List on 12.09.2023.

CRLR No. 520 of 2023
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
None is present for the revisionist.
2. Mr. S.C. Chauhan, learned D.A.G. 
alongwith Mr. Vikas Uniyal, learned Brief 
Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for
respondent no. 2.
4. There is a delay of 35 days in filing the 
present criminal revision. The grounds shown 
in the delay condonation application are 
sufficient to condone the delay. Accordingly, 
the Delay Condonation Application No. 2 of 
2023 is allowed. The delay in filing the 
criminal revision is hereby condoned.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent no. 
2 have submitted that there is another 
revision filed by the revisionist being CRLR 
No. 899 of 2025.
6. List this matter on 29.07.2026, 
alongwith CRLR No. 899 of 2025.
 (Alok Mahra J.) 16.06.2026
